overview:
New Jersey's fifth district carries a modest Democratic lean, and incumbent Josh Gottheimer enters the general election with every structural advantage. He has raised about $4.8 million and holds roughly $12.8 million on hand, while Republican Sean Kirrane has raised under $56,000 with about $8,000 available, leaving the challenger little capacity to communicate with voters. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency, and the money gap.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket price Gottheimer's chances around 92 to 95 percent, and the fundamentals point the same direction. An independent candidate is on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign activity. The race rates as Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty stemming from the absence of polling rather than any observed threat.
